name: Dermaplaning razor
lead: Dermaplaning is a form of mechanical exfoliation in which a single sharp blade is drawn lightly across the face to remove the top layer of dead skin cells and fine vellus hair, or peach fuzz. Home versions use small, single-blade facial razors, while professionals use a scalpel.
It is used to get a smoother skin surface, brighter look and more even makeup and skincare application.

paras: The blade, held at a shallow angle, shaves off the stratum corneum and vellus hair at skin level. The hair follicle is untouched, so hair regrows on its normal schedule, and exfoliation lets products absorb more easily.

Risks include nicks, irritation and breakouts, and it is not advised over active acne or inflamed skin. Hair does not grow back thicker or darker, but the effects last only a few weeks. I found no controlled trials, and the evidence comes from clinic and aesthetics sources, though the mechanism is physically straightforward. Use a clean blade to reduce infection risk.
